# Ghost-AOS Git-Bus Treaty — Measured Split q\*: State Change, Shape, Acceptance

## Model (symbols pinned)

Bus delivers fixed slots of `SLOT_RAW = 65536` bytes. Two consumer paths drain disjoint byte ranges of one target image:

- **Path P** (pack plane): `B_P` logical bytes pending.
- **Path H** (hot plane): `B_H` logical bytes pending.

Each path has a measured goodput `e_X` = useful payload bytes per granted slot (encoding overhead included), carried as `e_X_milli = round(e_X · 1000)`. Required slot counts:

```
N_P = ceil_div(1000·B_P, e_P_milli)      N_H = ceil_div(1000·B_H, e_H_milli)
```

The split is the arbitration ratio `q = (P grants) : (H grants)`. Co-termination (`T_P = T_H`) requires `q = N_P/N_H`, and substituting the N definitions:

```
q* = N_P / N_H = (e_H / e_P) · (B_P / B_H) = m · B_P / B_H ,   m := e_H / e_P
```

`q*` is latched as the reduced integer pair `(q_num, q_den) = reduce(N_P, N_H)`. The closed form `m·B_P/B_H` is the estimator; the latch is exact; the only divergence is ≤ 1 slot of ceil-slack per path (asserted, see A3).

---

## 1. Exact state change

Treaty epoch FSM: `PROBE → MEASURED → LATCHED → RUNNING → CLOSED`. One mutation site: the epoch record (§2) swapped by a single 128-bit-aligned CAS; `epoch_seq` incremented; prior record marked `SUPERSEDED`; new record appended to the log with CRC.

| Transition | Precondition | Postcondition (exact mutations) |
|---|---|---|
| `PROBE`→`MEASURED` | 64 probe slots granted strictly alternating P,H; accumulators `p_acc`, `h_acc` hold delivered payload bytes | `e_P_mlli ← div_round(p_acc·1000, 64)`; `e_H_milli ← div_round(h_acc·1000, 64)`; if either is 0 → `FALLBACK` (`degraded=1`, `e_*_milli = 100000`, i.e. raw slot) |
| `MEASURED`→`LATCHED` | `B_P`, `B_H` latched from manifests; both > 0 | `N_P, N_H` computed per §2 identities; `(q_num,q_den) ← reduce(N_P,N_H)`; `T_slots ← N_P+N_H`; `sched_ver ← 1`; record CRC'd and CAS-swapped |
| `LATCHED`→`RUNNING` | record state field flipped atomically | arbiter generator armed with `(i_P,i_H)=(0,0)`, `cursor_s=0` |
| per-slot (RUNNING) | generator rule §2 | exactly one of `i_P++` / `i_H++`; every 4096 slots a ledger batch `{base_slot, g_P_cnt, g_H_cnt, running_crc}` appended |
| `RUNNING`→`CLOSED` | `cursor_s == T_slots − 1` | `finish_slot_P`, `finish_slot_H` stamped from ledger; by the Lemma below these are `{T−2, T−1}` in some order; record sealed |

**Re-latch (RESYNC):** at every 2²⁰ slots, recompute `N_P', N_H'` from *remaining* bytes and current `e_*_milli`; if `reduce(N_P',N_H') ≠ (q_num,q_den)`, splice: CAS-update `q_*/N_*/T_slots`, reset generator cursors to current `i_P,i_H`, append AMEND record. Bounded drift correction; no data-plane effect.

---

## 2. Data shape (little-endian, packed, CRC-64/XZ over all preceding bytes)

```c
struct BusSplitEpoch {          // 96 bytes, one per epoch
  uint64_t epoch_id;            // monotonically increasing
  uint64_t B_P_bytes;           // logical bytes, path P (manifest)
  uint64_t B_H_bytes;           // logical bytes, path H (manifest)
  uint32_t e_P_milli;           // measured payload-bytes/slot × 1000, P
  uint32_t e_H_milli;           // measured payload-bytes/slot × 1000, H
  uint64_t N_P, N_H;            // projected slot counts (identities below)
  uint64_t q_num, q_den;        // q* = reduce(N_P, N_H) = m·B_P/B_H (reduced)
  uint64_t T_slots;             // N_P + N_H ; co-termination slot index
  uint16_t sched_ver;           // 1
  uint8_t  state;               // PROBE..CLOSED
  uint8_t  degraded;            // 1 if fallback e used
  uint32_t _pad;
  uint64_t finish_slot_P;       // valid at CLOSED; ∈ {T−2, T−1}
  uint64_t finish_slot_H;       // valid at CLOSED; ∈ {T−2, T−1}
  uint64_t crc64;               // CRC-64/XZ
};
```

Identities enforced at LATCH: `N_P == ceil_div(1000·B_P, e_P_milli)`, `N_H == ceil_div(1000·B_H, e_H_milli)`, `q_num·N_H' == q_den·N_P'` for the reduced form, `T_slots == N_P + N_H`.

**Schedule generator** (`sched_ver = 1`), O(1) per slot, u128 intermediates:

```text
at slot s, granted-so-far (i_P, i_H):
  if i_P == N_P      → grant H
  elif i_H == N_H    → grant P
  elif (i_P+1)·N_H < (i_H+1)·N_P → grant P     # strict <; tie → H
  else               → grant H
```

**Lemma (exact co-termination).** Every slot increments exactly one counter and guards prevent overrun, so after `T_slots` slots `(i_P, i_H) = (N_P, N_H)`. At slot `s = T−1`, total increments = `T−1`, so combined deficit = 1: one counter sits at `target−1`, the other at `target`. Therefore the final two grants land at slots `T−2` and `T−1` — the paths finish exactly one slot apart, the minimum the serial bus permits. ∎

---

## 3. Acceptance test — `TestSplitCoTermByteIdentity`

**Fixture.** `rng = ChaCha8(0x68057A11)`; corpus 96 MiB; partition `P_len = 61_440_000`, `H_len = 37_158_400`. Canonical reference `REF = SHA256(corpus ‖ canonical_partition_manifest)`. Injected measurements `e_P_milli = 60000`, `e_H_milli = 58982` (exercises `m ≠ 1`). Derived: `N_P = ceil_div(61_440_000·1000, 60000) = 1_024_000`, `N_H = ceil_div(37_158_400·1000, 58982) = 630_001` (verify), `T = 1_654_001`.

**Data plane (what byte-identity covers).** Every slot carries `{u8 path_bit, u64 offset, u32 len ≤ SLOT_RAW, payload[len]}`; offsets come from the partition manifest, not the scheduler. Writes go to the target image at `(path, offset)`. Hence byte-identity validates the data plane (no truncation, duplication, or reordering corruption), while A2 separately validates timing.

**Procedure + assertions:**

```text
run treaty to CLOSED over the fixture; then:

A1 schedule replay: regenerate grants from (q_num,q_den); at loop exit
   assert s == T−1 ∧ i_P == N_P ∧ i_H == N_H.
   Per-prefix drift: ∀s: |i_P(s) − (s+1)·N_P/T| < 1  (computed in u128).

A2 co-termination: assert {finish_slot_P, finish_slot_H} = {T−2, T−1}
   (set-equality; max == T−1).  [Lemma]

A3 split identity: assert reduce(q_num,q_den) == reduce(N_P,N_H);
   assert N_P == ceil_div(1000·B_P, e_P_milli) ∧ same for H;
   assert |q_num·(m_den·B_H) − q_den·(m_num·B_P)| ≤ q_den·m_den
          with (m_num,m_den) = reduce(e_H_milli, e_P_milli)   # ceil-slack bound

A4 BYTE-IDENTITY (headline):
   assert image.len() == corpus.len();
   assert SHA256(image) == REF;                        # whole-image
   additionally block-wise: every 4 KiB block equal.   # localizes any failure

A5 negative controls (prove A4 is sensitive, not vacuous):
   flip one bit in any single delivered slot  → SHA256(image) != REF;
   swap the offsets of one P-slot and one H-slot → != REF.

A6 determinism: run twice from identical fixture; assert the ledger
   CRC chains are identical (byte-identical run history).
```

Pass criterion: A1–A6 all green, including both negative controls failing as specified. Re-run the suite with `e_P_milli = e_H_milli = 100000` (`m = 1`, pure proportional split) and with a RESYNC forced mid-run at slot 2²⁰ — same pass set, same `REF`.

**Why this is airtight:** the generator's guards make co-termination a counting theorem, not an empirical outcome (A2 cannot flake); byte-identity is anchored to a manifest-addressed write plane, so the scheduler provably cannot alter content, only cadence — and A2 pins the cadence exactly.
